title: South Florida places that sound fake (but you can visit)
igCaption:
South Florida places that sound fake, but you can actually go 🤯

Coral Castle: one man carved it out of multi-ton stones
Stiltsville: houses on stilts in the middle of Biscayne Bay
Monkey Jungle: 300+ primates since 1933
Neptune Memorial Reef: an underwater city 40 feet down

Send this to the friend who'd actually go.

#Miami #SouthFlorida #MiamiThingsToDo #HiddenMiami

scenes.text: These South Florida places sound fake. But you can actually go to all of them.
scenes.caption: These South Florida places sound fake. But you can actually go to all of them.

scenes.text: Coral Castle, near Homestead. One man, Edward Leedskalnin, built it by himself. Stones weighing several tons each, carved into walls, tables, chairs and a sundial.
scenes.caption: Coral Castle, near Homestead. One man, Edward Leedskalnin, built it by himself. Stones weighing several tons each, carved into walls, tables, chairs and a sundial.

scenes.text: Stiltsville. Wooden houses on stilts, in the middle of Biscayne Bay. Crawfish Eddie built one in 1933, when gambling was legal a mile offshore.
scenes.caption: Stiltsville. Wooden houses on stilts, in the middle of Biscayne Bay. Crawfish Eddie built one in 1933, when gambling was legal a mile offshore.

scenes.text: Monkey Jungle, in South Miami-Dade. It started in 1933 with six monkeys set free in the forest. Now it's home to more than three hundred primates.
scenes.caption: Monkey Jungle, in South Miami-Dade. It started in 1933 with six monkeys set free in the forest. Now it's home to more than three hundred primates.

scenes.text: And off Key Biscayne, there's a city underwater. The Neptune Memorial Reef sits forty feet down. It has roads, benches and statues.
scenes.caption: And off Key Biscayne, there's a city underwater. The Neptune Memorial Reef sits forty feet down. It has roads, benches and statues.
